notes: Photoshop B&W mixer, measured on AE 2026 8 bpc, straight 8-bit colour: sort max >= mid >= min; gray = min + (mid - min) * W_secondary/100 + (max - mid) * W_primary/100, primary = weight of the max channel (Reds/Greens/Blues), secondary = weight of the complement of the min channel (min R -> Cyans, min G -> Magentas, min B -> Yellows); clamp 0..255 and round to 8 bits with exact .5 ties DOWN (black_white_1: 114.5 -> 114). Weights in % (-200..300). Without Tint: bit-exact (black_white_0 0 mismatches, incl. semi-transparent pixels). Tint (AE 7 = 1, AE 8 colour): the 8-bit gray is coloured like a W3C/PDF 'Color' blend of the tint colour (SetLum with luma 0.30/0.59/0.11, then ClipColor): exact in the midtones (gray ~35..242: gray + (13, -1, -33) for the default tint), but in the clipped shadows AE keeps the min channel at 1/255 (ClipColor gives 0) and in the clipped highlights it differs by 1 on the min channel -> 12.5k opaque pixels off by 1, a single pixel off by 2. Tested alternatives (Rec.601/709 luma, min target 1/255, pivot shifts, 16-bit) were not exact either. Semi-transparent pixels +-1 (premultiplied offline input).
